topic: Stable source-memory identity versus receiver-visible memory identity in a public ScienceWorld agent

sources.observed: GlobalMemory records source trajectories by env_idx/trial_idx and vector mode creates Chroma IDs as trial_idx_env_idx, but recall() returns split action-guidance summary strings rather than those stable source IDs.
Each inference step obtains known_obs_history and action_guidance_history from GlobalMemory.recall() and inserts those returned summaries into the inference prompt.
The dependency list does not pin a ScienceWorld package version.
The public ScienceWorld run script specifies trials/envs/model/agent/environment but no ScienceWorld revision or package version.

findings.claim: A memory backend can possess stable source IDs while the receiver-visible prompt loses identity: in public CDMem ScienceWorld code, trajectory IDs exist internally but recall() emits aggregated summary text. Therefore source-ID existence alone is insufficient for a fixed-selected-memory causal claim unless the selected receiver payload is explicitly bound back to source identities/digests.
findings.scope: Implementation-level observation for the inspected CDMem revision only; it does not imply the summaries are scientifically invalid or that CDMem performance claims are wrong.

findings.claim: The inspected CDMem ScienceWorld public run surface does not bind a ScienceWorld version in requirements or its run script, so exact environment-state replay requires an additional environment revision/JAR binding in any durable evidence packet.
findings.scope: Observed repository surface only; an external environment lockfile or unpublished run manifest is not excluded.
